claim.pdf_says: Figure E.4 — COBOL communication environment: a drawn diagram with four columns (COBOL Program box listing RECEIVE, RECEIVE, SEND, ..SEND, .....RECEIVE, SEND; a vertical 'Communication Descriptions (CD)' bar labelled 'COBOL/MCS Interface'; the Message Control System (MCS) with an 'Input Queues' box and an 'Output Queues' box, '(communication using queues)' and '(transaction communication)'; a vertical 'ENABLE / DISABLE' bar labelled 'MCS/Communication Device Interface'; and five Communication Devices), with arrows showing data flowing devices -> input queues -> RECEIVE, SEND -> output queues -> devices, and the transaction-communication RECEIVE/SEND paths bypassing the queues.

claim.why_it_matters: The figure was OCR'd into fragmentary tables: the arrows (all of the data-flow information), the device column and the CD and ENABLE/DISABLE bars are lost or scrambled ('Communication' and 'Descriptions' split into separate cells, 'ENABLE' duplicated, 'DISABLE' detached). The informative text on page 757 points the reader to this figure for the relationships among RECEIVE/SEND, the MCS queues and ENABLE/DISABLE; the markdown cannot convey them. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is lost.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 736 (PDF p758) shows Figure E.4 as described: the COBOL Program box (RECEIVE, RECEIVE, SEND, ..SEND, .....RECEIVE, SEND), the vertical 'Communication Descriptions (CD)' bar over 'COBOL/MCS Interface', Input Queues and Output Queues boxes under '(communication using queues)', '(transaction communication)', the vertical 'ENABLE / DISABLE' bar over 'MCS/Communication Device Interface', five terminal icons, and arrows running devices -> input queues -> RECEIVE, SEND -> output queues -> devices, plus a direct RECEIVE/SEND path between the program and the bottom device. The markdown breaks this into scattered tables: it has no arrows, so it carries none of the data flow. 'Communication' and 'Descriptions' land in different cells ('Communication ..SEND', 'Descriptions . . . Output Queues'), ENABLE appears twice and DISABLE stands apart, and the device images are gone. That loss of content is genuine for anyone reading the markdown alone. The figure is in informative Annex E, so it is structural and no normative rule is lost. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
